lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: entry requirements and training pathways

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic entry requirements and training pathways task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner researches what is actually required to start in the job (education level, certification, apprenticeship, or experience) and writes the pathway as a numbered sequence of steps in the order they would realistically happen, marking any step that depends on local rules.
safetyNotes: Requirements such as minimum age, licensing, or certification rules vary by location; the task explicitly asks the learner to flag anything that needs local verification rather than presenting one source as universally true.
materials: learner-local: research from the previous lesson

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What is the biggest difference between your warm-up guesses and the real pathway you found?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Pathway ordering: Steps are numbered in a mostly realistic order with at most one step out of place. | Local-verification awareness: At least one step is correctly flagged as depending on local rules. | Realistic time estimate: Gives a plausible total time estimate consistent with the pathway. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner research a second, faster or slower alternative pathway to the same job (for example, a certificate program instead of a full degree, or the reverse) and compare the time and requirement trade-offs between the two pathways.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: entry requirements and training pathways worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner researches what is actually required to start in the job (education level, certification, apprenticeship, or experience) and writes the pathway as a numbered sequence of steps in the order they would realistically happen, marking any step that depends on local rules.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact entry requirements and training pathways decision or action.
Model move 2: Before researching, list what you currently guess is required to start in this job.
Model move 3: Research the actual entry requirements and write them as a numbered sequence of steps in realistic order.

Model check: Pathway ordering: Steps are numbered in a mostly realistic order with at most one step out of place. | Local-verification awareness: At least one step is correctly flagged as depending on local rules. | Realistic time estimate: Gives a plausible total time estimate consistent with the pathway.

resources.title: entry requirements and training pathways action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for entry requirements and training pathways.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: entry requirements and training pathways coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner researches what is actually required to start in the job (education level, certification, apprenticeship, or experience) and writes the pathway as a numbered sequence of steps in the order they would realistically happen, marking any step that depends on local rules.
Coach direction: Before researching, list what you currently guess is required to start in this job.
Learner prompt: List your current guesses about what's required (education, certification, experience, or anything else).
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: entry requirements and training pathways complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Research the actual entry requirements and write them as a numbered sequence of steps in realistic order.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Write the pathway as numbered steps, from where someone starts to their first day in this job.
Response 2 (t2-p2): The steps are in a realistic order, not just a random list of requirements.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I marked at least one step that depends on local rules and needs to be verified rather than assumed.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: entry requirements and training pathways minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is the biggest difference between your warm-up guesses and the real pathway you found?

Success checks: Pathway ordering: Steps are numbered in a mostly realistic order with at most one step out of place. | Local-verification awareness: At least one step is correctly flagged as depending on local rules. | Realistic time estimate: Gives a plausible total time estimate consistent with the pathway.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: entry requirements and training pathways supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional entry requirements and training pathways condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Pathway ordering: Steps are numbered in a mostly realistic order with at most one step out of place. | Local-verification awareness: At least one step is correctly flagged as depending on local rules. | Realistic time estimate: Gives a plausible total time estimate consistent with the pathway..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: entry requirements and training pathways — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the entry requirements and training pathways task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: What is the biggest difference between your warm-up guesses and the real pathway you found?
observableCriteria: Pathway ordering: Steps are numbered in a mostly realistic order with at most one step out of place.
Local-verification awareness: At least one step is correctly flagged as depending on local rules.
Realistic time estimate: Gives a plausible total time estimate consistent with the pathway.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Pathway ordering: Steps are numbered in a mostly realistic order with at most one step out of place. | Local-verification awareness: At least one step is correctly flagged as depending on local rules. | Realistic time estimate: Gives a plausible total time estimate consistent with the pathway.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
